Are we made to be in the water?

🇺🇸 Yes, totally! Our bodies are fully adapted to it. The Mammalian Diving Reflex is a set of natural and unconscious responses we and mammalians have 🙌🏼

Essentially it’s a survival mechanism that allows us to hold our breath longer and dive deeper should we need to 🐋 It’s the same one that dolphins and whales have 🥰

We don’t have gills or fins but we have a special power 😎  

Remember this next time you go in the ocean 🌊

•

🇮🇹 Siamo fatti per stare in acqua?

Si, assolutamente! Il corpo umano è pienamente adattato. Il Riflesso del Mammifero è una serie di risposte naturali e subconscie che abbiamo, come tutti in mammiferi 🙌🏼

Essenzialmente è un meccanismo di sopravvivenza che ci permette di trattenere il fiato più a lungo e di immergerci più in profondità se ne abbiamo la necessità 🐋 É lo stesso che hanno i delfini e le balene 🥰

Non abbiamo branchie o pinne ma abbiamo un potere speciale 😎

Ricordatelo la prossima volta che vai al mare 🌊

good thing I’ve never been great at choosing.

I don’t want to choose between building a future I’m excited about and actually enjoying the life I have right now.

So yes, I’m doing my Master’s. I’m also living full time in a van with my dog, chasing waves when I can, waking up in different places and occasionally doing uni work from very questionable “offices”, while also traveling the world✈️

It’s definitely not the easiest or most conventional way to do it, but I think I’d rather make space for all the things that matter to me than convince myself I have to pick just one version of life.

We’re allowed to want both. And we’re allowed to figure out what “both” looks like for us.

A Guide to Paris …a story of taking your time, lingering over good food and always dressing for the occasion, told from the heart of @bvlgarihotelparis 

“Prendre son temps” A French way of saying… to take your time. Not because you have nothing to do but because some moments deserve a little longer...and Paris is one of them.

“Mettre les pieds sous la table” A French expression, literally to put your feet under the table. But the French never meant the furniture. It means to sit back while someone else takes care of everything.

“Se Mettre sur son 31” A French way of saying, literally to put yourself on your thirty-one. The French simply mean dress for the occasion and in Paris…the occasion is every evening.

This year I’m gonna prove them wrong🎬

Swipe across for the itinerary and more details below! 🚗 We went on an epic road trip with @VisitTheUSA to drive Route 66 for its 100th anniversary, also known as USA’s most iconic roadtrip and it definitely lived up to its name. Here’s how we spent our four days!

📍 Day 1: Albuquerque, New Mexico
We started in Albuquerque and explored Old Town and Nob Hill. We were meant to ride the Sandia Peak Tramway, but a storm rolled in so we’ll have to save it for next time!

📍 Day 2: Gallup, New Mexico
We then drove to the iconic town of Gallup. There are some amazing natural spots nearby like Church Rock at Red Rock Park, and Sandstone Bluffs Overlook on the way in. The town itself is super retro, and we stayed at the historic El Rancho Hotel, where old Hollywood western stars once stayed.

📍 Day 3: Petrified Forest National Park and Winslow, Arizona
Next up was Petrified Forest, and the rocks were insane! The landscapes were so unique and it was super quiet, which was such a nice change of pace. We then stopped by the iconic town of Winslow, which was a little rainy but still so worth the visit.

📍 Day 4: Las Vegas, Nevada
We finally made it to Las Vegas and caught sunrise on the Red Rock Canyon Scenic Drive, which is an absolute must do. It’s crazy how it is only 20 minutes from the Vegas Strip! We then hiked the Calico Tanks trail and finished off with an epic helicopter ride over the Strip and Red Rock Canyon for some seriously unique angles! 🚁

This was an incredible few days and I want to come back and do the whole thing!

Some of my favourite places in the video were Red Rock Canyon, Petrified Forest National Park and Albuquerque’s Old Town! I spent 4 days driving across 3 states on the most iconic road trip in the USA, Route 66, with @VisitTheUSA for its 100th anniversary.

I’ve spent the last couple months testing out this 3-5 stop magnetic variable filter around Europe and it’s been absolutely game changing to say the least. 

For those that don’t know, a VND is basically sunglasses for your camera.

It lets you control exposure without having to change your aperture or shutter speed, so you can still keep that natural motion blur even in harsh sunlight

A CPL helps cut reflections from things like glass, water, and shiny surfaces while also giving you cleaner colors and more contrast.

Together, they make a huge difference when you’re shooting outside

For this video I used the 82mm Magnetic CPL + VND3-5 Stop

Comment “ND” and I’ll share you a complete guide on these filters!
